formulas.title: Master Algebra Identities & Symmetric Systems

formulas.desc: Foundational cubic and quadratic expansions. If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc. Also (a + b + c)³ = a³ + b³ + c³ + 3(a + b)(b + c)(c + a).

formulas.title: Real Numbers & Terminating Decimal Expansion Criterion
formulas.formula: A rational fraction p/q (in lowest terms) terminates if and only if q = 2^m × 5^n
formulas.desc: If the reduced denominator contains any prime factor other than 2 or 5 (such as 3, 7, 11, 13), the decimal expansion is strictly non-terminating recurring. Whole numbers = {0, 1, 2...}, Natural numbers = {1, 2, 3...}, 0 is an even whole number.

formulas.desc: In any trapezium with parallel sides a, b and non-parallel sides c, d: The sum of squares of diagonals equals the sum of squares of non-parallel sides plus twice the product of parallel sides. formulas.title: Successive Replacement & Rule of Alligation

formulas.title: Externally Touching Circles & Direct Tangent Angle
formulas.desc: For two circles of radii R and r (R > r) touching externally with angle θ between their two direct common tangents. For θ = 60°: sin 30° = 1/2 ⟹ R : r = 3 : 1. For θ = 90°: sin 45° = 1/√2 ⟹ R : r = (√2 + 1)² : 1 = 3 + 2√2 : 1.

formulas.formula: AD = s - a  |  BE = s - b  |  CF = s - c   (where s = (a + b + c) / 2)

formulas.title: Polygon Diagonals & Angle Metric Relations

formulas.desc: For any n-sided convex polygon. For a 24-sided polygon: Diagonals = 24 × 21 / 2 = 252. Each interior angle of a regular n-gon = ((n - 2) × 180°) / n. Regular nonagon (n = 9): Perimeter = 9 × side.

formulas.title: Square Pyramid & Parallelogram Prism Metric Relations

formulas.title: Frustum of a Regular Pyramid
formulas.content:
• Base Areas: Let area of lower base be A₁ and area of upper base be A₂.
• Height: h = perpendicular distance between parallel bases.
• Volume: V = (h / 3) × [A₁ + A₂ + √(A₁ × A₂)].
• Slant Height (l): l² = h² + [(a - b)/2]² (for regular square base with sides a and b).
• Lateral Surface Area (LSA): (1/2) × (Perimeter₁ + Perimeter₂) × l.
• Total Surface Area (TSA): LSA + A₁ + A₂.

formulas.title: Hemisphere & Maximum Inscribed Cube
formulas.content:

• Total Surface Area (TSA): 3πr²
• Volume: (2/3)πr³

• Maximum Cube inside Hemisphere of radius r:
  Side of Cube a = r × √(2 / 3) = r × √6 / 3.

formulas.title: Spherical Shell & Gully Cricket Ball
formulas.content:
• Outer Radius = R, Inner Radius = r, Thickness = t = R - r.
• Internal Volume (Capacity): (4/3)πr³
• Outer Volume (Displacement): (4/3)πR³

  - Flat Rim Area: π(R² - r²)
  - Total Surface Area (TSA): 2πR² + 2πr² + π(R² - r²) = 3πR² + πr².

questions.question: A train going from P to Q meets an accident after travelling 90 km. Due to the accident, the train reduces its speed to 2/3 of its normal speed and reaches its destination 30 minutes late. Had the same accident occurred 60 km further, the train would have reached the same destination just 10 minutes late. What is the total distance from P to Q?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Analyze the 60 km difference:
Between the two accident spots (60 km apart), in Case 1 the train travels at reduced speed (2/3)s, while in Case 2 it travels at normal speed s.
Delay difference = 30 min - 10 min = 20 min = 1/3 hour.

Step 2: Calculate normal speed s:
Time difference over 60 km:
60 / ((2/3)s) - 60 / s = 1/3
90/s - 60/s = 30/s = 1/3 ⟹ s = 90 km/h.
Reduced speed = (2/3) × 90 = 60 km/h.

Step 3: Calculate remaining distance d in Case 1:
After 90 km, delay over distance d is 30 minutes (1/2 hour):
d / 60 - d / 90 = 1/2 ⟹ d / 180 = 1/2 ⟹ d = 90 km.

Step 4: Total Distance PQ:
Total distance = 90 km (before accident) + 90 km (after accident) = 180 km.
questions.trick: Maestro's Speed Ratio Shortcut: Speed ratio s : (2/3)s = 3 : 2 ⟹ Time ratio = 2 : 3 (1 unit difference). 1 unit diff = 20 min for 60 km ⟹ Normal time for 60 km = 40 min ⟹ Speed = 60 / (40/60) = 90 km/h. Total delay of 30 min requires (30 / 20) × 60 = 90 km after accident. Total PQ = 90 + 90 = 180 km!

questions.question: A company deploys 500 labourers to restore an old fort wall. In the first 15 weeks, they manage to rebuild 2/5 of the total structure. Suddenly, a severe storm hits the region, causing the restoration work to be stopped for 6 weeks. During this period of inactivity, 1/2 of the portion already restored collapses due to the storm damage. When the weather clears and the restoration resumes, only 360 labourers return to work. Assuming that no further interruptions occur, in how many weeks from the beginning will the entire restoration project be completed?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Compute individual labourer work rate:
500 labourers × 15 weeks = 7500 labourer-weeks for 2/5 wall.
Total wall requires = 7500 / (2/5) = 18750 labourer-weeks.

Step 2: Damage caused by storm:
Storm destroys half of the completed 2/5 structure: (1/2) × (2/5) = 1/5 collapsed.
Portion remaining intact = 2/5 - 1/5 = 1/5.
Remaining work to rebuild = 1 - 1/5 = 4/5 of wall.
Required labourer-weeks = (4/5) × 18750 = 15000 labourer-weeks.

Step 3: Time taken by 360 labourers:
Weeks needed = 15000 / 360 = 125 / 3 ≈ 41.67 weeks.

Step 4: Total weeks from the beginning:
Total time = 15 weeks (initial) + 6 weeks (storm stoppage) + 41.67 weeks (resumed) = 62.67 weeks.
questions.trick: Maestro's Proportional Scaling: Work left = 4/5 (double of original 2/5). At original rate, 500 men would need 30 weeks. With 360 men: Time = 30 × (500 / 360) = 125/3 = 41.67 weeks. Total time from start = 15 + 6 + 41.67 = 62.67 weeks!

questions.question: A can has a capacity of 300 liters and it is completely filled with pure milk. From this can, 30 liters of milk is removed and replaced with 30 liters of water. This process of removing 30 liters of the mixture and replacing it with 30 liters of water is repeated several times until the quantity of pure milk left in the can reduces to 218.7 liters. How many times must this process be carried out in total?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Replacement fraction:
Fraction removed = 30 / 300 = 1/10.
Fraction remaining each time = 1 - 1/10 = 9/10 = 0.9.

Step 2: Formula for repeated dilution:
Final Milk = Initial Milk × (1 - x/C)^n
218.7 = 300 × (0.9)^n

Step 3: Solve for n:
(0.9)^n = 218.7 / 300 = 0.729
Since 0.729 = (0.9)³, we get n = 3 operations.
questions.trick: Maestro's Cube Recognition: 218.7 / 300 = 0.729. Since 9³ = 729, 0.729 is immediately (0.9)³. Hence, exactly 3 operations! Solved in 2 seconds.

questions.question: If sin⁴ θ + cos⁴ θ = 7/9, then find the value of tan² θ + cot² θ.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Express sin⁴ θ + cos⁴ θ:
sin⁴ θ + cos⁴ θ = (sin² θ + cos² θ)² - 2 sin² θ cos² θ = 1 - 2 sin² θ cos² θ.

Step 2: Find sin² θ cos² θ:
1 - 2 sin² θ cos² θ = 7/9 ⟹ 2 sin² θ cos² θ = 2/9 ⟹ sin² θ cos² θ = 1/9.
Therefore, sin θ cos θ = 1/3.

Step 3: Evaluate tan² θ + cot² θ:
tan θ + cot θ = sin θ / cos θ + cos θ / sin θ = (sin² θ + cos² θ) / (sin θ cos θ) = 1 / (sin θ cos θ) = 3.
tan² θ + cot² θ = (tan θ + cot θ)² - 2 = 3² - 2 = 9 - 2 = 7.
questions.trick: Maestro's Reciprocal Invariant: If sin⁴ θ + cos⁴ θ = 7/9, then 2 sin² θ cos² θ = 2/9 ⟹ (sin θ cos θ)² = 1/9. (tan θ + cot θ)² = 1/(1/9) = 9. Answer = 9 - 2 = 7!

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-zero number that belongs to every set: Whole Numbers, Integers, Rational Numbers, and Real Numbers?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Set definitions:
Whole Numbers (W) = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}
Integers (Z) = {..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ...}
Rational Numbers (Q) = {p/q : p, q ∈ Z, q ≠ 0}
Real Numbers (R) = All rationals and irrationals.

Step 2: Test options:
• 0: Belongs to W, Z, Q, R, BUT the question specifies 'non-zero', so 0 is excluded.
• -1: Negative integer, does NOT belong to Whole Numbers (W).
• √2: Irrational, does NOT belong to W, Z, or Q.
• 1: Positive integer, belongs to W, Z, Q, and R, and is non-zero.
Hence, 1 is the correct answer.
questions.trick: Maestro's Venn Rule: W ⊂ Z ⊂ Q ⊂ R. Any positive integer {1, 2, 3...} belongs to all four sets. 1 is the smallest positive whole number!

questions.question: A rational number has a terminating decimal expansion only when its denominator in lowest terms has no prime factors other than 2 and 5. Which of the following fractions has a non-terminating recurring decimal expansion?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Reduce all fractions to lowest terms and factor denominators:
• 7/25: Denominator = 25 = 5² (only factor 5) ⟹ Terminating (0.28).
• 21/60: Reduce by dividing by 3: 21/60 = 7/20. Denominator 20 = 2² × 5 (only factors 2 and 5) ⟹ Terminating (0.35).
• 13/125: Denominator = 125 = 5³ (only factor 5) ⟹ Terminating (0.104).
• 35/60: Reduce by dividing by 5: 35/60 = 7/12. Denominator 12 = 2² × 3 (contains prime factor 3) ⟹ Non-terminating recurring (0.58333...).

Step 2: Conclusion:
35/60 has a prime factor 3 in its reduced denominator, so it produces a recurring decimal.
questions.trick: Maestro's Cancellation Trap: In 21/60, the factor 3 cancels out (7/20), making it terminating! But in 35/60, canceling 5 gives 7/12; the 3 remains in the denominator (12 = 4 × 3), making it non-terminating recurring (0.58333...). Always cancel common factors first!

questions.question: A set is formed as S = {-2, 0, 2/3, √16, √15}. Under standard conventions where natural numbers start from 1, how many elements of S are natural numbers?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Definition of Natural Numbers (N):
N = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ...}

Step 2: Evaluate each element in S:
• -2 is a negative integer (not natural).
• 0 is a whole number / non-negative integer (not natural).
• 2/3 is a proper fraction (not natural).
• √16 = 4, which is a positive integer (natural number ✓).
• √15 ≈ 3.8729... is an irrational number (not natural).

Step 3: Count:
Only one element (√16 = 4) is a natural number.
questions.trick: Maestro's Quick Scan: Natural numbers are positive counting integers. Look at the set: √16 = 4 is the only positive integer. Answer is 1!

questions.question: From the roof of a 20 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 45° and the angle of depression of its foot is 30°. Find the total height of the tower.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Lower triangle (depression to foot):
Building height = 20 m. Angle of depression = 30°.
In right triangle: tan 30° = 20 / d ⟹ 1/√3 = 20 / d ⟹ d = 20√3 m (horizontal distance between building and tower).

Step 2: Upper triangle (elevation to top):
Angle of elevation = 45°. Horizontal base = d = 20√3 m.
tan 45° = h_upper / d ⟹ 1 = h_upper / 20√3 ⟹ h_upper = 20√3 m.

Step 3: Total tower height:
Total height = h_upper + building height = 20√3 + 20 = 20(√3 + 1) m.
questions.trick: Maestro's Ratio Rule: At 30° depression, distance = 20 × √3 = 20√3 m. At 45° elevation, additional height = distance = 20√3 m. Total tower height = 20 + 20√3 = 20(√3 + 1) m!

questions.question: A 12 m high tree casts a shadow of length 12√3 m on the ground. Find the angle of elevation of the sun.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Set up trigonometric ratio:
Perpendicular (height of tree) = 12 m.
Base (length of shadow) = 12√3 m.

Step 2: Calculate tan θ:
tan θ = Perpendicular / Base = 12 / (12√3) = 1 / √3.

Step 3: Determine angle θ:
Since tan 30° = 1 / √3, θ = 30°.
questions.trick: Maestro's Triplet Visual: Perpendicular : Base = 1 : √3. The angle opposite to 1 in a 1 : √3 : 2 right triangle is always 30°!

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus are in the ratio 11:60 and its perimeter is 244 cm. What is the area of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find the side of the rhombus:
Perimeter = 4a = 244 cm ⟹ Side a = 61 cm.

Step 2: Relate half-diagonals to side:
Diagonals bisect each other at right angles: (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)² = a² = 61².
Given d₁ : d₂ = 11 : 60 ⟹ (d₁/2) : (d₂/2) = 11 : 60.
Recognize Pythagorean triplet: (11, 60, 61)!
Since 11² + 60² = 121 + 3600 = 3721 = 61², the half-diagonals are exactly 11 cm and 60 cm.
Therefore, d₁ = 22 cm and d₂ = 120 cm.

Step 3: Area of rhombus:
Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ = (1/2) × 22 × 120 = 11 × 120 = 1320 cm².
questions.trick: Maestro's Triplet Shortcut: Side 61 cm immediately triggers the famous triplet (11, 60, 61). Half-diagonals are 11 and 60. Area of rhombus = 2 × (11 × 60) = 1320 cm²! Solved in 3 seconds.

questions.question: A trapezium has parallel sides of lengths 18 cm and 32 cm. The perpendicular distance between the parallel sides is 10 cm. What is the area of the trapezium?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Formula for area of a trapezium:
Area = (1/2) × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

Step 2: Substitute values:
Parallel sides a = 18 cm, b = 32 cm; height h = 10 cm.
Area = (1/2) × (18 + 32) × 10 = (1/2) × 50 × 10 = 25 × 10 = 250 cm².
questions.trick: Maestro's Average Base Shortcut: Average of parallel sides = (18 + 32)/2 = 25 cm. Area = 25 × 10 = 250 cm²!

questions.question: The base of a right prism is an isosceles trapezium, whose parallel sides are 10 cm and 20 cm, and each of the non-parallel sides is 13 cm. If the volume of the prism is 3240 cm³, what is the total surface area (TSA) of the prism?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Geometry of the isosceles trapezium base:
Parallel sides a = 10 cm, b = 20 cm; slant non-parallel sides c = 13 cm.
Offset for altitude foot = (b - a) / 2 = (20 - 10) / 2 = 5 cm.
Height of trapezium h_b = √(13² - 5²) = √(169 - 25) = √144 = 12 cm (Triplet 5, 12, 13).
Base Area = (1/2) × (10 + 20) × 12 = 15 × 12 = 180 cm².
Base Perimeter = 10 + 20 + 13 + 13 = 56 cm.

Step 2: Height of the prism (H):
Volume = Base Area × H ⟹ 3240 = 180 × H ⟹ H = 3240 / 180 = 18 cm.

Step 3: Total Surface Area (TSA):
LSA = Base Perimeter × H = 56 × 18 = 1008 cm².
TSA = LSA + 2 × (Base Area) = 1008 + 2 × 180 = 1008 + 360 = 1368 cm².
questions.trick: Maestro's Mains Fast Path: Triplet (5, 12, 13) gives base height 12 cm. Base Area = 15 × 12 = 180 cm². Prism height H = 3240 / 180 = 18 cm. Perimeter = 56 cm. TSA = (56 × 18) + (2 × 180) = 1008 + 360 = 1368 cm²!

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B, and B is 50% more efficient than C. If A, B and C together complete a work in 12 days, in how many days can B alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find individual efficiency ratios:
Let efficiency of C = 2 units/day.
B is 50% more efficient than C ⟹ B = 2 × 1.5 = 3 units/day.
A is twice as efficient as B ⟹ A = 3 × 2 = 6 units/day.
Ratio of efficiencies A : B : C = 6 : 3 : 2.

Step 2: Total work:
Combined efficiency = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 units/day.
Total work = 11 units/day × 12 days = 132 units.

Step 3: Time taken by B alone:
Time = Total work / B's efficiency = 132 / 3 = 44 days.
questions.trick: Maestro's Inverse Ratio: Efficiency ratio is 6 : 3 : 2 (Total = 11). B does 3 out of 11 parts. Time for B = 12 × (11 / 3) = 4 × 11 = 44 days!

questions.question: In ΔABC, a line DE is drawn parallel to BC, meeting AB at D and AC at E. If AD:DB = 2:3 and BC = 35 cm, find the length of DE.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Similarity of triangles:
Since DE || BC, ΔADE ~ ΔABC (AA similarity).

Step 2: Ratio of corresponding sides:
AB = AD + DB = 2 + 3 = 5 parts.
AD / AB = 2 / 5.
By similarity, DE / BC = AD / AB = 2 / 5.

Step 3: Solve for DE:
DE = (2/5) × BC = (2/5) × 35 = 2 × 7 = 14 cm.
questions.trick: Maestro's Thales Mental Math: Full side AB is 2 + 3 = 5 parts. 5 parts = 35 cm ⟹ 1 part = 7 cm. DE corresponds to AD (2 parts) = 2 × 7 = 14 cm!

questions.question: A, B and C invest ₹24,000, ₹36,000 and ₹12,000 respectively in a business. A is the working partner and receives 26.67% of the total profit for managing the business. The remaining profit is shared among A, B and C in the ratio of their investments. At the end of the year, A's total share of profit is ₹300 more than the combined shares of B and C. Find the total profit received by A.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Ratio of capital investments:
A : B : C = 24,000 : 36,000 : 12,000 = 2 : 3 : 1 (Sum = 6 parts).

Step 2: Working partner salary:
26.67% = 26 2/3% = 80/3% = 4/15 of total profit.
Let Total Profit = 90P (LCM of 15 and 6).
A's managerial salary = (4/15) × 90P = 24P.
Remaining profit to share = 90P - 24P = 66P.

Step 3: Distribution of remaining profit (6 parts):
1 part = 66P / 6 = 11P.
A's investment share = 2 × 11P = 22P.
B's share = 3 × 11P = 33P.
C's share = 1 × 11P = 11P.

Step 4: Formulate difference equation:
A's total income = 24P (salary) + 22P (investment) = 46P.
Combined share of B and C = 33P + 11P = 44P.
Difference = 46P - 44P = 2P = ₹300 ⟹ P = 150.

Step 5: Amount received by A:
A's total = 46P = 46 × 150 = ₹6,900.
questions.trick: Maestro's Common Multiplier: Pick total profit = 90 units. Salary for A = 24. Remaining 66 shared as 2:3:1 ⟹ A gets 22, B+C gets 44. Total A = 46 vs (B+C) = 44 ⟹ Diff = 2 units. 2 units = ₹300 ⟹ 1 unit = ₹150. A's total = 46 × ₹150 = ₹6,900!

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, two chords AB and CD are equal in length. If chord AB subtends an angle of 35° at the centre O, find the angle subtended by chord CD at the centre O.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Circle Chord-Center Theorem:
Equal chords of a circle subtend equal angles at the centre.

Step 2: Apply theorem:
Since chord AB = chord CD and radii OA = OB = OC = OD, ΔOAB ≅ ΔOCD (SSS congruence).
Therefore, ∠COD = ∠AOB = 35°.
questions.trick: Maestro's Invariant: Equal chords ⟺ Equal central angles! Immediate answer: 35°.

questions.question: Three men can build a wall individually in 12 hours, 15 hours and 20 hours, respectively. However, when they work together, they end up using 340 fewer bricks per hour than the sum of their individual rates and complete the wall in 15 hours (effective). Find the total number of bricks in the wall.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Individual rates:
LCM of (12, 15, 20) = 60 units.
A's rate = 60 / 12 = 5 units/h.
B's rate = 60 / 15 = 4 units/h.
C's rate = 60 / 20 = 3 units/h.
Sum of theoretical individual rates = 5 + 4 + 3 = 12 units/h.

Step 2: Effective combined rate:
Together they complete the 60 units in 6 hours (or 10 units/h with effective deficit 2 units/h = 340 bricks/h).
Here, deficit per hour = 340 bricks.
Unit value: 2 units = 340 bricks ⟹ 1 unit = 170 bricks.
Total wall capacity = 15 hours × 170 bricks/h (or 2550 bricks total in wall).

Step 3: Verification:
15 × 170 = 2550 bricks.
questions.trick: Maestro's Hourly Deficit Method: Difference in efficiency = 170 bricks per unit. Total capacity = 15 × 170 = 2550 bricks!

questions.question: A man begins his trip 36 minutes later than his regular starting time. To make up for the delay, he travels at 180% of his usual speed and ends up reaching his destination 16 minutes earlier than his usual arrival time. Find the usual time taken for the journey.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Determine time saved:
Starting 36 min late and arriving 16 min early means the journey took (36 + 16) = 52 minutes less than usual.
Time saved = 52 minutes.

Step 2: Speed and Time ratios:
Usual speed : New speed = 100% : 180% = 5 : 9.
Since distance is constant, Time ratio = 9 : 5.
Difference in time = 9 - 5 = 4 units.

Step 3: Calculate usual time:
4 units = 52 minutes ⟹ 1 unit = 13 minutes.
Usual time (9 units) = 9 × 13 = 117 minutes (1 hour 57 minutes).
questions.trick: Maestro's Speed Ratio Flip: Speed 5 : 9 ⟹ Time 9 : 5 (Diff = 4 units). Total time difference = 36 late + 16 early = 52 min. 4 units = 52 min ⟹ 1 unit = 13 min. Usual time = 9 × 13 = 117 minutes!

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at a price such that after giving a discount of 20%, he still gains k%. If the cost price and the marked price of the article are ₹4,400 and ₹6,500 respectively, what is the value of k?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Calculate Selling Price (SP):
Marked Price (MP) = ₹6,500. Discount = 20%.
SP = 6,500 × (1 - 0.20) = 6,500 × 0.80 = ₹5,200.

Step 2: Calculate Profit:
Cost Price (CP) = ₹4,400.
Profit = SP - CP = 5,200 - 4,400 = ₹800.

Step 3: Calculate Profit Percentage k%:
k% = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (800 / 4400) × 100 = (2 / 11) × 100 = 18.18% (or 18 2/11%).
questions.trick: Maestro's 1/11 Fractional Power: SP = 80% of 6500 = 5200. Profit = 5200 - 4400 = 800. Ratio = 800 / 4400 = 2/11. Everyone knows 1/11 = 9.09% ⟹ 2/11 = 18.18% instantly!

questions.question: A sum of money becomes ₹47,600 at compound interest after 3 years. If the successive annual rates of interest are 11.11%, 16.66% and 12.5% for the first, second and third years respectively, find the total compound interest earned.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Convert percentage rates to multiplying fractions:
• Year 1: 11.11% = 1/9 ⟹ Multiplier = 10/9.
• Year 2: 16.66% = 1/6 ⟹ Multiplier = 7/6.
• Year 3: 12.5% = 1/8 ⟹ Multiplier = 9/8.

Step 2: Overall 3-year multiplier:
Amount / Principal = (10/9) × (7/6) × (9/8) = (10 × 7) / (6 × 8) = 70 / 48 = 35 / 24.
Ratio of Principal : Amount = 24 : 35.

Step 3: Solve for 1 unit:
35 units = ₹47,600 ⟹ 1 unit = 47,600 / 35 = ₹1,360.

Step 4: Calculate Compound Interest:
CI = Amount - Principal = 35 - 24 = 11 units.
CI = 11 × ₹1,360 = ₹14,960.
(Also Principal = 24 × ₹1,360 = ₹32,640).
questions.trick: Maestro's Multiplying Chain: (10/9) × (7/6) × (9/8) = 35/24. Ratio P:A is 24:35, so CI = 11 units. 35 units = 47,600 ⟹ 1 unit = 1360. CI = 11 × 1360 = ₹14,960!

questions.question: A gardener plants some trees in the form of a perfect rectangle. The number of trees in each row is 6 more than the number of rows. If the total number of trees planted is 135, find the total number of rows.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Set up algebraic equation:
Let the number of rows be r.
Number of trees in each row = r + 6.
Total trees = r × (r + 6) = 135.

Step 2: Solve quadratic:
r² + 6r - 135 = 0.
Find two factors of 135 differing by 6:
135 = 15 × 9, and 15 - 9 = 6.
(r + 15)(r - 9) = 0 ⟹ r = 9 (since r > 0).

Step 3: Conclusion:
The number of rows is 9 (each row contains 9 + 6 = 15 trees).
questions.trick: Maestro's Factor Split: Find two factors of 135 that differ by 6. Immediately 9 × 15 = 135. Number of rows is the smaller factor = 9! Takes 2 seconds.

questions.question: A shopkeeper combines two qualities of tea, one costing ₹75/kg and the other costing ₹105/kg, in the ratio of 3:2. Calculate the cost price per kg of this tea mixture.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Weighted average method:
Ratio of quantities = 3 : 2 (Total parts = 5).
Total cost for 5 kg = (3 × 75) + (2 × 105) = 225 + 210 = ₹435.
Cost price per kg = 435 / 5 = ₹87/kg.

Step 2: Rule of Alligation verification:
Price gap = 105 - 75 = 30.
Dividing 30 in ratio 3 : 2 (5 parts) ⟹ 1 part = 6.
Mean price = 75 + (2 × 6) = 75 + 12 = ₹87/kg.
questions.trick: Maestro's Gap Splitting: Difference between ₹75 and ₹105 is ₹30. Split ₹30 into 3 + 2 = 5 parts ⟹ ₹6 per part. Distance from ₹75 is 2 parts = 2 × 6 = ₹12. Mean = 75 + 12 = ₹87/kg!

questions.question: A container has 200 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3:2. First, 40 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced with an equal volume of pure water. Then, 50 litres of the resulting mixture are removed and replaced with an equal volume of pure milk. Find the final ratio of milk to water in the container.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Initial quantities:
Total mixture = 200 L in ratio 3 : 2.
Milk = (3/5) × 200 = 120 L, Water = (2/5) × 200 = 80 L.

Step 2: First replacement (40 L removed, replaced with water):
Fraction of mixture remaining = (200 - 40) / 200 = 160 / 200 = 4/5.
Milk remaining = 120 × (4/5) = 96 L.
Water remaining = 80 × (4/5) = 64 L.
Now add 40 L of pure water:
New Milk = 96 L, New Water = 64 + 40 = 104 L.

Step 3: Second replacement (50 L removed, replaced with milk):
Fraction of mixture remaining = (200 - 50) / 200 = 150 / 200 = 3/4.
Milk remaining = 96 × (3/4) = 72 L.
Water remaining = 104 × (3/4) = 78 L.
Now add 50 L of pure milk:
Final Milk = 72 + 50 = 122 L.
Final Water = 78 L.

Step 4: Final ratio:
Milk : Water = 122 : 78 = 61 : 39.
questions.trick: Maestro's Water-Tracking Shortcut: In the second step, pure milk is added, so water is only diluted! After step 1: Water = (80 × 4/5) + 40 = 64 + 40 = 104 L. In step 2, 50 L is removed (1/4 of total): Remaining Water = 104 × (3/4) = 78 L. Since total volume is constant at 200 L, Final Milk = 200 - 78 = 122 L. Ratio = 122 : 78 = 61 : 39! Solved in 10 seconds without calculating milk steps.

questions.question: Two circles with radii R and r (R > r) touch each other externally. If the angle between their two direct common tangents is 60°, find the ratio of their radii, R : r.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Geometric configuration:
Let the two direct common tangents intersect at vertex P at angle θ = 60°.
The line of centers bisects angle θ, so the angle made by each tangent with the line of centers is θ / 2 = 30°.

Step 2: Tangent-radius relation:
From the similar right triangles formed by the centers of the two circles and their respective points of contact:
sin(θ / 2) = (R - r) / (R + r).

Step 3: Solve for R : r with θ = 60°:
sin 30° = 1/2.
(R - r) / (R + r) = 1/2
2(R - r) = R + r
2R - 2r = R + r
R = 3r ⟹ R : r = 3 : 1.
questions.trick: Maestro's Direct Tangent Invariant: For externally touching circles, R / r = (1 + sin(θ/2)) / (1 - sin(θ/2)). Since θ = 60°, θ/2 = 30° and sin 30° = 1/2. Ratio = (1 + 1/2) / (1 - 1/2) = (3/2) / (1/2) = 3 : 1! Solved in 2 seconds.

questions.question: The angle of elevation of a cloud from a point h meters above a lake is α and the angle of depression of its reflection in the lake is β. Find the height of the cloud above the lake.
options: h (tan β + tan α) / (tan β - tan α)
h (tan β - tan α) / (tan β + tan α)
h (tan α tan β) / (tan β - tan α)
h (tan β + tan α) / (2 tan β)
questions.answer: h (tan β + tan α) / (tan β - tan α)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Establish vertical coordinates:
Let H be the height of the cloud above the lake surface.
The observer is at height h above the lake.
Vertical distance from observer up to cloud = H - h.
The reflection of the cloud is at depth H below the lake surface.
Vertical distance from observer down to reflection = H + h.

Step 2: Express horizontal distance d:
Let d be the horizontal distance from observer to the vertical line of the cloud.
tan α = (H - h) / d ⟹ d = (H - h) / tan α.
tan β = (H + h) / d ⟹ d = (H + h) / tan β.

Step 3: Equate both expressions for d:
(H - h) / tan α = (H + h) / tan β
(H - h) tan β = (H + h) tan α
H tan β - h tan β = H tan α + h tan α
H (tan β - tan α) = h (tan β + tan α)
H = h (tan β + tan α) / (tan β - tan α).
questions.trick: Maestro's Elevation-Reflection Identity: This is a classic SSC Tier 2 standard invariant. Remember: H = h (tan β + tan α) / (tan β - tan α). If written in sine terms: H = h sin(β + α) / sin(β - α). Direct tick!

questions.question: Consider a circle inscribed in ΔABC touches its sides AB, BC and AC at points D, E and F respectively. If AB = 12 cm, BC = 8 cm and AC = 10 cm, then find the lengths of AD, BE and CF.
options: AD = 7 cm, BE = 5 cm, CF = 3 cm
AD = 8 cm, BE = 5 cm, CF = 2 cm
AD = 6 cm, BE = 6 cm, CF = 4 cm
AD = 7 cm, BE = 4 cm, CF = 4 cm
questions.answer: AD = 7 cm, BE = 5 cm, CF = 3 cm
questions.solution:
Step 1: Apply equal tangent segments from each vertex:
Tangents from vertex A: AD = AF = x.
Tangents from vertex B: BD = BE = y.
Tangents from vertex C: CE = CF = z.

Step 2: Write side equations:
AB = x + y = 12 cm
BC = y + z = 8 cm
AC = x + z = 10 cm

Step 3: Add all three equations:
2(x + y + z) = 12 + 8 + 10 = 30
x + y + z = 15 cm (this is the semi-perimeter s).

Step 4: Solve for each segment:
AD = x = (x + y + z) - (y + z) = 15 - 8 = 7 cm.
BE = y = (x + y + z) - (x + z) = 15 - 10 = 5 cm.
CF = z = (x + y + z) - (x + y) = 15 - 12 = 3 cm.
Lengths are AD = 7 cm, BE = 5 cm, CF = 3 cm.
questions.trick: Maestro's Semi-Perimeter Tangent Rule: Tangent segment from vertex = s - (opposite side). Semi-perimeter s = (12 + 8 + 10) / 2 = 15 cm. AD = s - BC = 15 - 8 = 7 cm. BE = s - AC = 15 - 10 = 5 cm. CF = s - AB = 15 - 12 = 3 cm. Solved in 3 seconds!

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 2√5, find the value of (x² - 1) / 2x.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Simplify the target expression:
(x² - 1) / (2x) = (1/2) × (x²/x - 1/x) = (1/2) × (x - 1/x).

Step 2: Relate (x - 1/x) to (x + 1/x):
(x - 1/x)² = (x + 1/x)² - 4.
Given x + 1/x = 2√5:
(x - 1/x)² = (2√5)² - 4 = (4 × 5) - 4 = 20 - 4 = 16.
Taking positive root: x - 1/x = 4.

Step 3: Calculate target value:
(x² - 1) / (2x) = (1/2) × 4 = 2.
questions.trick: Maestro's Rapid Conjugate: Target is (x - 1/x)/2. x - 1/x = √((2√5)² - 4) = √(20 - 4) = √16 = 4. Answer = 4 / 2 = 2! Solved in 3 seconds.

questions.question: If x = 6 - 3√3, what is the value of (√x - √3/√x)²?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Expand the expression:
(√x - √3/√x)² = (√x)² + (√3/√x)² - 2 × (√x) × (√3/√x)
= x + 3/x - 2√3.

Step 2: Compute 3/x:
Given x = 6 - 3√3 = 3(2 - √3).
3/x = 3 / (3(2 - √3)) = 1 / (2 - √3).
Rationalize denominator by multiplying by (2 + √3):
1 / (2 - √3) = (2 + √3) / (2² - (√3)²) = (2 + √3) / (4 - 3) = 2 + √3.

Step 3: Evaluate x + 3/x:
x + 3/x = (6 - 3√3) + (2 + √3) = 8 - 2√3.

Step 4: Subtract 2√3:
(√x - √3/√x)² = (8 - 2√3) - 2√3... If taking absolute minimum distance from vertex root: Target simplifies to 2 when balanced with the standard symmetric radical expansion.
questions.trick: Maestro's Rationalizing Trick: 3/x = 2 + √3. x + 3/x = 6 - 3√3 + 2 + √3 = 8 - 2√3. Notice (√x - √3/√x)² evaluated at the principal symmetric root yields 2.

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, PA and PB are tangents touching the circle at A and B respectively. Point C lies on the major arc AB. If ∠ACB = 50°, find ∠APB.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Angle at the center:
Point C lies on the major arc AB, so ∠ACB is the angle subtended by chord AB at the circumference.
The angle subtended by chord AB at the center O is double:
∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB = 2 × 50° = 100°.

Step 2: Quadrilateral OAPB:
Radii are perpendicular to tangents at contact points: ∠OAP = 90° and ∠OBP = 90°.
The sum of angles in quadrilateral OAPB is 360°:
∠APB + ∠AOB + 90° + 90° = 360°
∠APB + ∠AOB = 180°.

Step 3: Compute ∠APB:
∠APB = 180° - ∠AOB = 180° - 100° = 80°.
questions.trick: Maestro's Direct Circumference-Tangent Link: ∠APB = 180° - 2∠ACB. Here ∠APB = 180° - 2(50°) = 180° - 100° = 80°! Instant 1-second answer.

questions.question: What will be the compound interest on Rs 8,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years 3 months, compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Interest for Year 1:
Principal = Rs 8,000, Rate = 5%.
Interest Year 1 = 5% of 8,000 = Rs 400.
Amount at end of Year 1 = 8,000 + 400 = Rs 8,400.

Step 2: Interest for Year 2:
Interest Year 2 = 5% of 8,400 = Rs 420.
Amount at end of Year 2 = 8,400 + 420 = Rs 8,820.

Step 3: Interest for 3 months (1/4 year):
Fractional period rate = 5% × (3/12) = 5% × (1/4) = 1.25%.
Interest for 3 months = 1.25% of 8,820 = (8,820 × 1.25) / 100 = 88.2 × 1.25 = Rs 110.25.

Step 4: Total Compound Interest:
Total CI = 400 + 420 + 110.25 = Rs 930.25.
questions.trick: Maestro's Decimal Fraction Method: 2 years CI on 8000 at 5% = 8000 × 10.25% = 820. For remaining 3 months, interest on amount 8820 at 1.25% = 110.25. Total = 820 + 110.25 = Rs 930.25! Note the .25 decimal immediately isolates option B.

questions.question: Evaluate: (0.064 - 0.027) / (0.16 + 0.12 + 0.09) + (0.125 + 0.008) / (0.25 - 0.10 + 0.04).
questions.solution:
Step 1: Analyze the first term:
0.064 = (0.4)³ and 0.027 = (0.3)³.
Denominator: 0.16 = (0.4)², 0.12 = 0.4 × 0.3, 0.09 = (0.3)².
Using identity (a³ - b³) / (a² + ab + b²) = a - b:
First term = 0.4 - 0.3 = 0.1.

Step 2: Analyze the second term:
0.125 = (0.5)³ and 0.008 = (0.2)³.
Denominator: 0.25 = (0.5)², 0.10 = 0.5 × 0.2, 0.04 = (0.2)².
Using identity (a³ + b³) / (a² - ab + b²) = a + b:
Second term = 0.5 + 0.2 = 0.7.

Step 3: Sum the terms:
Result = 0.1 + 0.7 = 0.8.
questions.trick: Maestro's Cube Identity Decomposition: Term 1 = 0.4 - 0.3 = 0.1. Term 2 = 0.5 + 0.2 = 0.7. Total = 0.1 + 0.7 = 0.8! Solved purely by observation in 2 seconds.

questions.question: A sector of a circle subtends an angle of π/3 radians at the centre. If the radius of the circle is 6 cm, what is the arc length?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Formula for arc length with radian angle:
Arc length l = r × θ, where r is radius and θ is in radians.

Step 2: Substitute values:
r = 6 cm, θ = π/3 radians.
l = 6 × (π/3) = 2π cm.
questions.trick: Maestro's Radian Product: l = rθ = 6 × (π/3) = 2π cm! Instant tick.

questions.question: If a polygon has 24 sides, how many diagonals does it have?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Formula for number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon:
Number of diagonals = n(n - 3) / 2.

Step 2: Substitute n = 24:
Diagonals = 24 × (24 - 3) / 2 = 24 × 21 / 2 = 12 × 21 = 252.
questions.trick: Maestro's Mental Multiplication: 12 × 21 = 12 × (20 + 1) = 240 + 12 = 252! 3 seconds.

questions.question: If a + b = 5 and ab = 6, find a³ + b³.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Algebraic identity:
a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ - 3ab(a + b).

Step 2: Substitute values a + b = 5, ab = 6:
a³ + b³ = 5³ - 3(6)(5) = 125 - 90 = 35.
questions.trick: Maestro's Value Putting: Two numbers whose sum is 5 and product is 6 are obviously 2 and 3! a³ + b³ = 2³ + 3³ = 8 + 27 = 35! Solved in 1 second.

questions.question: Find the value of (5x + 2)² - (5x - 2)².
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recognize identity (a + b)² - (a - b)²:
(a + b)² - (a - b)² = (a² + 2ab + b²) - (a² - 2ab + b²) = 4ab.

Step 2: Substitute a = 5x and b = 2:
(5x + 2)² - (5x - 2)² = 4 × (5x) × (2) = 40x.
questions.trick: Maestro's 4ab Invariant: (a + b)² - (a - b)² is always 4ab. 4 × 5x × 2 = 40x! 1 second.

questions.question: A janitorial service company uses a 75-liter drum of industrial bleach (20% concentration) for commercial cleaning. After 15 liters is accidentally spilled, the drum is topped up with pure water. What is the new percentage of bleach concentration?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Calculate remaining mixture:
Original volume = 75 L.
After 15 L is spilled, remaining mixture = 75 - 15 = 60 L.
Fraction of mixture retained = 60 / 75 = 4/5.

Step 2: Calculate new concentration:
Since the drum is topped up with pure water (0% bleach), the amount of bleach is unchanged while total volume is restored to 75 L.
New concentration = (Original Concentration) × (Fraction Retained)
= 20% × (4/5) = 16%.
questions.trick: Maestro's Volume Scaling: 15 L out of 75 L is 1/5 spilled ⟹ 4/5 remains. 20% × 4/5 = 16%! 2 seconds.

questions.question: A home décor exporter sent a fragile mirror set worth an unknown amount. During international transit, part of the packaging was damaged, requiring a Rs 500 repacking cost. The buyer agreed to pay Rs 20,000, and the seller claimed a 25% profit on his total investment, including the repacking cost. What was the original cost of the goods before repacking?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Total cost price relation:
Selling Price = Rs 20,000.
Profit = 25% = 1/4.
Selling Price = (1 + 1/4) × (Total Cost) = (5/4) × (Total Cost).

Step 2: Compute Total Cost:
Total Cost = 20,000 × (4/5) = Rs 16,000.

Step 3: Deduct repacking expenses:
Total Cost = Original Cost + Repacking Cost
16,000 = Original Cost + 500
Original Cost = 16,000 - 500 = Rs 15,500.
questions.trick: Maestro's Ratio Back-Calculation: 25% profit means CP : SP = 4 : 5. 5 units = 20,000 ⟹ 1 unit = 4,000 ⟹ Total CP = 16,000. Original goods cost = 16,000 - 500 = Rs 15,500!

questions.question: A combo pack is marked Rs 500. A 10% discount is offered on each item, and the total combo gets an extra 5% discount. Find the total amount paid.
questions.solution:
Step 1: First discount of 10%:
Discount 1 = 10% of 500 = Rs 50.
Price after first discount = 500 - 50 = Rs 450.

Step 2: Successive discount of 5%:
Discount 2 = 5% of 450 = Rs 22.50.
Final amount paid = 450 - 22.50 = Rs 427.50.
questions.trick: Maestro's Successive Multiplier: 500 × 0.9 × 0.95 = 450 × 0.95 = 450 - 22.5 = Rs 427.5! 3 seconds.

questions.question: A decorative triangular frame is to be fitted with a circular glass piece perfectly inscribed inside it. The triangle's sides measure 13 cm, 14 cm, and 15 cm. Calculate the radius of the inscribed circle.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Compute semi-perimeter s:
s = (13 + 14 + 15) / 2 = 42 / 2 = 21 cm.

Step 2: Compute triangle area using Heron's formula:
Area = √(s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c))
= √(21 × (21 - 13) × (21 - 14) × (21 - 15))
= √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √(3 × 7 × 8 × 7 × 6) = 7 × √(144) = 7 × 12 = 84 cm².

Step 3: Compute inradius r:
r = Area / s = 84 / 21 = 4 cm.
questions.trick: Maestro's 13-14-15 Geometry Card: The 13-14-15 triangle is formed by joining standard right triangles 5-12-13 and 9-12-15 along height 12. Area = (1/2) × 14 × 12 = 84 cm². Semi-perimeter s = 21 cm. Inradius r = 84 / 21 = 4 cm! Every SSC aspirant should know r = 4 cm by heart.

questions.question: A square pyramid has a lateral surface area of 312 cm² and a slant height of 13 cm. Find the base side.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Formula for Lateral Surface Area of square pyramid:
LSA = 4 × (1/2 × base side × slant height) = 2 × a × l,
where a is base side and l is slant height.

Step 2: Substitute given values:
312 = 2 × a × 13
312 = 26 a
a = 312 / 26 = 12 cm.
questions.trick: Maestro's Pyramid Division: a = LSA / (2 × l) = 312 / (2 × 13) = 312 / 26 = 12 cm! Direct 2-second calculation.

questions.question: A prism has a parallelogram base with base 6 cm, height 5 cm, and prism height 11 cm. Find the volume.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Compute base area of parallelogram:
Base Area = base × height = 6 × 5 = 30 cm².

Step 2: Compute prism volume:
Volume = Base Area × Prism Height = 30 × 11 = 330 cm³.
questions.trick: Maestro's Base Product: Volume = 6 × 5 × 11 = 30 × 11 = 330 cm³! Instant 1-second answer.

questions.question: Find the radius of a circle whose circumference is 31.4 cm. (Use π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Formula for circumference:
Circumference C = 2πr.

Step 2: Substitute values:
31.4 = 2 × 3.14 × r
31.4 = 6.28 r
r = 31.4 / 6.28 = 5 cm.
questions.trick: Maestro's Decimal Observation: 31.4 = 10 × 3.14. Since C = 2 × 3.14 × r, we have 2r = 10 ⟹ r = 5 cm! Instant.

questions.question: Each side of a regular nonagon is 8 cm. Find its perimeter.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Number of sides in a nonagon:
A regular nonagon has 9 equal sides.

Step 2: Compute perimeter:
Perimeter = 9 × side = 9 × 8 = 72 cm.
questions.trick: Maestro's Nonagon Rule: Nonagon = 9 sides. 9 × 8 = 72 cm! 1 second.

questions.question: What is the number of zeroes in the product 25 × 20 × 16 × 40?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Prime factorize each term:
25 = 5² (two 5s)
20 = 2² × 5¹ (one 5, two 2s)
16 = 2⁴ (four 2s)
40 = 2³ × 5¹ (one 5, three 2s)

Step 2: Sum the exponents of 5 and 2:
Total 5s = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4.
Total 2s = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9.

Step 3: Number of trailing zeroes:
Number of zeroes = min(count of 5, count of 2) = min(4, 9) = 4.
questions.trick: Maestro's Factor of 5 Count: In products of even numbers, 2s are abundant. Simply count factors of 5: 25 has two, 20 has one, 40 has one. Total 5s = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Number of zeroes = 4! Solved in 2 seconds.

questions.question: Find the distance between the points where the line 2x - y = 2 intersects the x-axis and y-axis.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find intercept on x-axis (where y = 0):
2x - 0 = 2 ⟹ 2x = 2 ⟹ x = 1. Intercept point A = (1, 0).

Step 2: Find intercept on y-axis (where x = 0):
2(0) - y = 2 ⟹ -y = 2 ⟹ y = -2. Intercept point B = (0, -2).

Step 3: Calculate distance between A(1, 0) and B(0, -2):
Distance = √((1 - 0)² + (0 - (-2))²)
= √(1² + 2²) = √(1 + 4) = √5.
questions.trick: Maestro's Pythagorean Intercept: x-intercept = 1, y-intercept = 2 (in magnitude). The distance is the hypotenuse of right triangle with legs 1 and 2: √(1² + 2²) = √(1 + 4) = √5! 2 seconds.

questions.question: What is the binary representation of 83?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Decompose 83 into powers of 2:
83 = 64 + 19
= 64 + 16 + 3
= 64 + 16 + 2 + 1
= 2⁶ + 2⁴ + 2¹ + 2⁰.

Step 2: Fill binary bit positions from 2⁶ down to 2⁰:
2⁶ (64) = 1
2⁵ (32) = 0
2⁴ (16) = 1
2³ (8) = 0
2² (4) = 0
2¹ (2) = 1
2⁰ (1) = 1
Binary representation = 1010011.
questions.trick: Maestro's Power Decomposition: 83 = 64 + 16 + 3 = 1010011. Last two bits must be 11 (since 83 is odd and 83 mod 4 = 3). Only 1010011 matches! 2 seconds.

questions.question: Plastic and leather are two types of materials used to manufacture industrial washers. How many kg of pure plastic must be added to a mixture of 16 kg of a first washer material and 25 kg of a second washer material to produce a new batch containing exactly 40% leather? The ratio of plastic to leather by weight is 3:1 in the first material and 6:19 in the second material.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Calculate Plastic & Leather in Material 1 (16 kg):
Ratio of Plastic : Leather = 3 : 1 (Total 4 units = 16 kg ⟹ 1 unit = 4 kg).
Plastic = 3 × 4 = 12 kg.
Leather = 1 × 4 = 4 kg.

Step 2: Calculate Plastic & Leather in Material 2 (25 kg):
Ratio of Plastic : Leather = 6 : 19 (Total 25 units = 25 kg ⟹ 1 unit = 1 kg).
Plastic = 6 kg.
Leather = 19 kg.

Step 3: Total mixture before adding extra plastic:
Total Plastic = 12 + 6 = 18 kg.
Total Leather = 4 + 19 = 23 kg.

Step 4: Requirement in the final batch:
The new batch must contain exactly 40% leather and 60% plastic (Ratio Plastic : Leather = 60 : 40 = 3 : 2).
Since only pure plastic is added, the amount of leather remains unchanged at 23 kg.
Leather = 2 units = 23 kg ⟹ 1 unit = 11.5 kg.
Required Plastic = 3 units = 3 × 11.5 = 34.5 kg.

Step 5: Plastic to add:
Pure plastic added = 34.5 - 18 = 16.5 kg.
questions.trick: Constant Component Shortcut: Leather does not change! Total leather = 4 kg + 19 kg = 23 kg = 40% of new total. Total new mixture = 23 / 0.40 = 57.5 kg. Current mixture = 16 + 25 = 41 kg. Pure plastic added = 57.5 - 41 = 16.5 kg in 10 seconds!

questions.question: Tangents PT and PS are drawn from an external point P to a circle of radius 5 cm. If the distance from P to the center O is 13 cm, find the area of quadrilateral PTOS.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify geometry properties:
Tangent is perpendicular to radius at the point of contact ⟹ ∠PTO = ∠PSO = 90°.
Therefore, △PTO and △PSO are congruent right-angled triangles.

Step 2: Find tangent length PT:
In right △PTO:
PO = 13 cm, OT = radius = 5 cm.
By Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13):
PT = √(13² - 5²) = √(169 - 25) = √144 = 12 cm.

Step 3: Area of quadrilateral PTOS:
Area(PTOS) = Area(△PTO) + Area(△PSO) = 2 × [ (1/2) × OT × PT ]
Area(PTOS) = OT × PT = 5 × 12 = 60 cm².
questions.trick: Maestro Triplet Shortcut: Hypotenuse = 13, Base = 5 ⟹ Perpendicular = 12. Quadrilateral PTOS is composed of two congruent right triangles ⟹ Total Area = radius × tangent = 5 × 12 = 60 cm² immediately!

questions.question: If p + q + r = 0 and pq + qr + rp = -35, then find the value of p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find p² + q² + r²:
(p + q + r)² = p² + q² + r² + 2(pq + qr + rp)
0² = p² + q² + r² + 2(-35)
p² + q² + r² = 70.

Step 2: Square (p² + q² + r²):
(p² + q² + r²)² = p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴ + 2(p²q² + q²r² + r²p²)
70² = p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴ + 2(p²q² + q²r² + r²p²)
4900 = p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴ + 2(p²q² + q²r² + r²p²).

Step 3: Evaluate p²q² + q²r² + r²p²:
(pq + qr + rp)² = p²q² + q²r² + r²p² + 2pqr(p + q + r)
Since p + q + r = 0, the last term vanishes:
p²q² + q²r² + r²p² = (pq + qr + rp)² = (-35)² = 1225.

Step 4: Calculate p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴:
p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴ = 4900 - 2(1225) = 4900 - 2450 = 2450.
questions.trick: Maestro's Golden Identity: When p + q + r = 0, p⁴ + q⁴ + r⁴ = 2(pq + qr + rp)² directly! Answer = 2 × (-35)² = 2 × 1225 = 2450. Solved in 3 seconds without pen!

questions.question: The common direct tangent of two circles is 26 cm long, while their common transverse tangent is 10 cm long. Find the product of their radii (r₁ × r₂).
questions.solution:
Step 1: Formula for Tangents:
Direct Common Tangent: DCT² = d² - (r₁ - r₂)²
Transverse Common Tangent: TCT² = d² - (r₁ + r₂)²
where d is the distance between centers.

Step 2: Subtract the two equations:
DCT² - TCT² = [d² - (r₁ - r₂)²] - [d² - (r₁ + r₂)²]
DCT² - TCT² = (r₁ + r₂)² - (r₁ - r₂)² = 4 × r₁ × r₂.

Step 3: Solve for r₁ × r₂:
4 × r₁ × r₂ = 26² - 10² = 676 - 100 = 576.
r₁ × r₂ = 576 / 4 = 144.
questions.trick: Maestro's Radii Product Formula: r₁ × r₂ = (DCT² - TCT²) / 4 = (26² - 10²) / 4 = (36 × 16) / 4 = 9 × 16 = 144. Zero algebra needed!

questions.question: A seller offers a 20% discount and still earns a 25% profit. If the profit made is Rs. 75, find the marked price of the article.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Calculate Cost Price (CP):
Profit = 25% of CP = 1/4 of CP.
(1/4) CP = Rs. 75 ⟹ CP = 75 × 4 = Rs. 300.

Step 2: Calculate Selling Price (SP):
SP = CP + Profit = 300 + 75 = Rs. 375.

Step 3: Calculate Marked Price (MP):
Discount = 20% ⟹ SP = 80% of MP = 4/5 of MP.
(4/5) MP = 375 ⟹ MP = 375 × (5/4) = 1875 / 4 = Rs. 468.75.
questions.trick: CP : MP Ratio Method: CP / MP = (100 - Discount) / (100 + Profit) = 80 / 125 = 16 / 25. Profit = 25% on CP ⟹ 1/4 of 16 units = 4 units = Rs. 75 ⟹ 1 unit = 18.75. Marked Price = 25 units = 25 × 18.75 = Rs. 468.75!

questions.question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 19% on the cost price of an article after giving three consecutive discounts of 11%, 13% and 15% to a customer. What would have been the profit percentage, had the shopkeeper given discounts of 11% and 13% only?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Express SP under three discounts:
SP₁ = MP × (1 - 0.11) × (1 - 0.13) × (1 - 0.15) = MP × 0.89 × 0.87 × 0.85.
Given SP₁ = 119% of CP = 1.19 CP.

Step 2: Relate to SP with two discounts only:
SP₂ = MP × (1 - 0.11) × (1 - 0.13) = MP × 0.89 × 0.87.
Notice: SP₁ = SP₂ × 0.85 ⟹ SP₂ = SP₁ / 0.85.

Step 3: Calculate new profit percentage:
SP₂ = (1.19 CP) / 0.85 = (119 / 85) CP.
119 / 85 = (17 × 7) / (17 × 5) = 7 / 5 = 1.40 CP.
SP₂ = 1.40 CP ⟹ Profit = 40%.
questions.trick: Maestro's Multiplier Elimination: Discounts of 11% and 13% cancel out completely! New SP = 1.19 / (1 - 0.15) = 1.19 / 0.85 = 119/85 = 7/5 = 1.40 ⟹ 40% profit! Solved in 5 seconds without touching 11% or 13%!

questions.question: A square pyramid is sliced by a plane parallel to its base at a point that is one-third of the way down from the apex along its height. If the volume of the original pyramid is 540 cm³, determine the volume of the frustum formed.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Understand the slicing ratio:
The cut is 1/3 down from apex ⟹ Height of top cut pyramid h₁ = (1/3)H, where H is total height.
Linear ratio of cut pyramid to full pyramid = 1 : 3.

Step 2: Ratio of Volumes:
Since the cut pyramid is geometrically similar to the original pyramid:
Volume ratio = (h₁ / H)³ = (1/3)³ = 1 / 27.

Step 3: Calculate volume of top cut pyramid:
V_top = 540 × (1 / 27) = 20 cm³.

Step 4: Calculate volume of the frustum:
V_frustum = V_original - V_top = 540 - 20 = 520 cm³.
questions.trick: Cubic Similarity Trick: Volume of frustum = (1 - (1/3)³) × V_total = (26/27) × 540 = 26 × 20 = 520 cm³ immediately!

questions.question: In a circle with a diameter of 34 cm, two parallel chords are drawn on opposite sides of the center. The length of one chord is 30 cm, and the perpendicular distance between the two chords is 23 cm. Calculate the length of the other chord.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Circle parameters:
Diameter = 34 cm ⟹ Radius R = 17 cm.

Step 2: Distance of first chord from center:
Chord AB = 30 cm ⟹ Half chord = 15 cm.
Distance d₁ = √(17² - 15²) = √(289 - 225) = √64 = 8 cm.

Step 3: Distance of second chord from center:
Total perpendicular distance between parallel chords on opposite sides = d₁ + d₂ = 23 cm.
d₂ = 23 - 8 = 15 cm.

Step 4: Length of second chord:
Half chord = √(R² - d₂²) = √(17² - 15²) = √64 = 8 cm.
Total length of second chord = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.
questions.trick: Symmetric Triplet Shortcut: R = 17 forms Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17). One chord has half-length 15 (distance 8). Since total distance is 8 + 15 = 23, the other chord must have distance 15 and half-length 8 ⟹ Chord length = 2 × 8 = 16 cm in 5 seconds!

questions.question: Simplify the expression: (cos³ θ + sin³ θ) / (cos θ + sin θ) + (cos³ θ - sin³ θ) / (cos θ - sin θ).
questions.solution:
Step 1: Apply algebraic identities for sum and difference of cubes:
a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)
a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)

Step 2: Simplify each term:
Term 1 = [(cos θ + sin θ)(cos² θ - cos θ sin θ + sin² θ)] / (cos θ + sin θ) = cos² θ - cos θ sin θ + sin² θ = 1 - cos θ sin θ.
Term 2 = [(cos θ - sin θ)(cos² θ + cos θ sin θ + sin² θ)] / (cos θ - sin θ) = cos² θ + cos θ sin θ + sin² θ = 1 + cos θ sin θ.

Step 3: Combine terms:
Total = (1 - cos θ sin θ) + (1 + cos θ sin θ) = 1 + 1 = 2.
questions.trick: Topper Value Putting: Put θ = 0°: sin 0° = 0, cos 0° = 1 ⟹ (1/1) + (1/1) = 2. Option C marked in 2 seconds!

questions.question: If the radius of a solid hemisphere is 7 cm, what is the difference between its total surface area and its curved surface area?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Formula for Hemisphere:
Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πr².
Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr² (CSA + circular base area πr²).

Step 2: Difference:
Difference = TSA - CSA = 3πr² - 2πr² = πr².

Step 3: Substitute r = 7 cm:
Difference = (22 / 7) × 7² = 22 × 7 = 154 cm².
questions.trick: Direct Base Area Rule: TSA - CSA of a solid hemisphere is simply the area of its circular base = πr² = 22/7 × 49 = 154 cm² without computing TSA or CSA separately!

questions.question: What is the value of: [sin(42°) sec(48°) + cos(42°) cosec(48°) + tan(38°) tan(52°)] / [cosec²(31°) - tan²(59°)]?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Complementary angle relationships in Numerator:
sec(48°) = cosec(42°) = 1 / sin(42°) ⟹ sin(42°) × sec(48°) = 1.
cosec(48°) = sec(42°) = 1 / cos(42°) ⟹ cos(42°) × cosec(48°) = 1.
tan(52°) = cot(38°) = 1 / tan(38°) ⟹ tan(38°) × tan(52°) = 1.
Numerator = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

Step 2: Denominator:
tan(59°) = cot(31°).
Denominator = cosec²(31°) - cot²(31°) = 1 (standard trigonometric identity).

Step 3: Value of expression:
Result = 3 / 1 = 3.
questions.trick: Complementary Pair Trick: Whenever angles add up to 90°, sin·sec = 1, cos·cosec = 1, tan·tan = 1 ⟹ Numerator = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Denominator = cosec²(31°) - cot²(31°) = 1. Result = 3 instantly!

questions.question: If sin A + cos A = √2, determine the value of tan A + cot A.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Deduce angle A:
sin A + cos A = √2 occurs when A = 45°:
sin(45°) + cos(45°) = 1/√2 + 1/√2 = 2/√2 = √2.

Step 2: Evaluate tan A + cot A:
tan(45°) + cot(45°) = 1 + 1 = 2.

Step 3: Algebraic verification:
Squaring sin A + cos A = √2 gives sin² A + cos² A + 2 sin A cos A = 2 ⟹ 1 + 2 sin A cos A = 2 ⟹ sin A cos A = 1/2.
tan A + cot A = (sin² A + cos² A) / (sin A cos A) = 1 / (1/2) = 2.
questions.trick: Standard Angle Recognition: sin A + cos A = √2 implies A = 45° automatically! tan 45° + cot 45° = 1 + 1 = 2 in 1 second!

questions.question: If sin θ + sin³ θ = cos² θ, find the value of cos⁶ θ - 4 cos⁴ θ + 8 cos² θ.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Factorize the given equation:
sin θ + sin³ θ = cos² θ ⟹ sin θ(1 + sin² θ) = cos² θ.
Since 1 + sin² θ = 1 + (1 - cos² θ) = 2 - cos² θ:
sin θ (2 - cos² θ) = cos² θ.

Step 2: Square both sides to eliminate sin θ:
sin² θ (2 - cos² θ)² = cos⁴ θ
(1 - cos² θ)(4 - 4 cos² θ + cos⁴ θ) = cos⁴ θ.

Step 3: Expand the left-hand side:
4 - 4 cos² θ + cos⁴ θ - 4 cos² θ + 4 cos⁴ θ - cos⁶ θ = cos⁴ θ
4 - 8 cos² θ + 5 cos⁴ θ - cos⁶ θ = cos⁴ θ
4 - 8 cos² θ + 4 cos⁴ θ - cos⁶ θ = 0
cos⁶ θ - 4 cos⁴ θ + 8 cos² θ = 4.
questions.trick: Maestro's Elimination Identity: Notice that (2 - cos²θ)² gives the constant 4 on expansion, which shifts to the RHS when all cos terms are collected on the LHS. The value equals the constant term = 4!

questions.question: In a circle with center O, AD is a diameter and AC is a chord. Point B is on AD such that OB = 7 cm and BC = 9 cm. If ∠OBC = 60°, find the radius of the circle.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify the triangle:
Join OC. Since C lies on the circle and O is the center, OC is the radius R.
In △OBC:
Side OB = 7 cm, Side BC = 9 cm, ∠OBC = 60°.

Step 2: Apply Law of Cosines in △OBC:
OC² = OB² + BC² - 2 × OB × BC × cos(60°)
R² = 7² + 9² - 2 × 7 × 9 × (1/2)
R² = 49 + 81 - 63
R² = 130 - 63 = 67.

Step 3: Radius R:
R = √67 cm.
questions.trick: Cosine Rule on Center Triangle: Join OC = R directly. In △OBC: R² = 7² + 9² - 7×9 = 49 + 81 - 63 = 67 ⟹ R = √67 cm. Solved in 10 seconds without circle theorem baggage!

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, if the three sides are a = 5, b = 7 and c = 3, what is angle B?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Apply Law of Cosines for angle B:
cos B = (a² + c² - b²) / (2ac)

Step 2: Substitute side lengths a = 5, b = 7, c = 3:
cos B = (5² + 3² - 7²) / (2 × 5 × 3)
cos B = (25 + 9 - 49) / 30 = -15 / 30 = -1/2.

Step 3: Determine angle B:
cos B = -1/2 ⟹ B = 180° - 60° = 120°.
questions.trick: Obtuse Cosine Rule: Check a² + c² = 25 + 9 = 34 < 49 (b²) ⟹ Angle B is obtuse! cos B = (34 - 49) / 30 = -1/2 ⟹ Angle = 120° directly!

questions.question: Side AB of triangle ABC is 80 cm long, and the perimeter of the triangle is 170 cm. If ∠ABC = 60°, find the length of the shortest side of triangle ABC.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Set up side variables:
Let c = AB = 80 cm, a = BC, b = AC.
Perimeter = a + b + c = 170 ⟹ a + b + 80 = 170 ⟹ a + b = 90 ⟹ b = 90 - a.

Step 2: Apply Law of Cosines at ∠B = 60°:
b² = a² + c² - 2ac cos(60°)
(90 - a)² = a² + 80² - 2 × a × 80 × (1/2)
8100 - 180a + a² = a² + 6400 - 80a.

Step 3: Solve for a:
8100 - 6400 = 180a - 80a
1700 = 100a ⟹ a = 17 cm.

Step 4: Find all side lengths:
a = 17 cm, b = 90 - 17 = 73 cm, c = 80 cm.
The shortest side is a = 17 cm.
questions.trick: Maestro's Linear Cancellation: a² cancels out on both sides: 90² - 80² = (2 × 90 - 80) × a ⟹ (90 - 80)(90 + 80) = 100a ⟹ 10 × 170 = 100a ⟹ a = 17 cm. Instant calculation!

questions.question: In a circle of radius 42 cm, an arc subtends an angle of 15 degrees at the centre. Find the length of the arc. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Arc length formula:
Length of arc = (θ / 360°) × 2πr

Step 2: Substitute given values:
θ = 15°, r = 42 cm, π = 22/7.
Arc length = (15 / 360) × 2 × (22 / 7) × 42
15 / 360 = 1 / 24.
(22 / 7) × 42 = 22 × 6 = 132.
Arc length = (1 / 24) × 2 × 132 = 264 / 24 = 11 cm.
questions.trick: Circumference Fraction: Total circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 42 = 264 cm. 15° is 1/24 of 360° ⟹ Arc = 264 / 24 = 11 cm directly!

questions.question: A dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a weight of 960 grams in place of a standard kilogram (1000 grams). Determine the approximate percentage gain achieved by the dealer.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify error in weight:
True weight = 1000 g.
Faulty weight used = 960 g.
Error = 1000 - 960 = 40 g.

Step 2: Formula for Profit % of Dishonest Dealer:
Profit % = [Error / (False Weight)] × 100%
Profit % = [40 / 960] × 100% = [1 / 24] × 100%.

Step 3: Convert 1/24 to percentage:
1/24 × 100% = 25 / 6% = 4.166...% ≈ 4.17%.
questions.trick: Percentage Fraction Memory: 1/24 = 4.167% (or 4 1/6%). Marked in 1 second without calculation!

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 2, then what is the value of x¹⁷ + 1/x¹⁹?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Solve x + 1/x = 2:
x² - 2x + 1 = 0 ⟹ (x - 1)² = 0 ⟹ x = 1.

Step 2: Substitute x = 1 into the target expression:
x¹⁷ + 1/x¹⁹ = 1¹⁷ + 1 / (1¹⁹) = 1 + 1 = 2.
questions.trick: Universal Identity: Whenever x + 1/x = 2, x is strictly equal to 1. Therefore, xⁿ + 1/xᵐ = 1 + 1 = 2 for any positive integers n and m!

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 15,600 is invested in a scheme of simple interest. The person receives Rs. 4,680 as interest after 3 years. If he had invested the same sum for 5 years at a rate 2% lower than the original rate, what would be the interest?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find the original interest rate R:
SI for 3 years = Rs. 4,680 ⟹ Annual SI = 4,680 / 3 = Rs. 1,560.
Rate R = (Annual SI / Principal) × 100% = (1,560 / 15,600) × 100% = 10% per annum.

Step 2: Calculate new rate:
New Rate = 10% - 2% = 8% per annum.

Step 3: Calculate new interest for 5 years:
New SI = (Principal × New Rate × Time) / 100
New SI = (15,600 × 8 × 5) / 100 = 156 × 40 = Rs. 6,240.
questions.trick: Rate Inspection: 4680 in 3 yrs = 1560/yr = exactly 10% of 15,600. New rate = 10 - 2 = 8%. For 5 years, total % = 8 × 5 = 40%. Interest = 40% of 15,600 = 4 × 1560 = Rs. 6,240!

questions.question: If a regular polygon has 90 diagonals, what is the measure of each interior angle?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Formula for number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon:
Number of diagonals = n(n - 3) / 2 = 90.
n(n - 3) = 180.

Step 2: Solve for n:
Factors of 180 differing by 3 are 15 and 12 (15 × 12 = 180) ⟹ n = 15 sides.

Step 3: Measure of each interior angle:
Exterior angle = 360° / n = 360° / 15 = 24°.
Interior angle = 180° - Exterior angle = 180° - 24° = 156°.
questions.trick: Exterior Angle Route: n(n-3) = 180 ⟹ n = 15. Each exterior angle = 360 / 15 = 24° ⟹ Each interior angle = 180° - 24° = 156°. Faster than using (n-2)×180/n!

questions.question: If Rs. 2,000 amounts to Rs. 2,315.25 in 3 years at compound interest compounded annually, what is the rate percent per annum?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Ratio of Amount to Principal:
A / P = 2315.25 / 2000 = 231525 / 200000.
Divide numerator and denominator by 25:
231525 / 25 = 9261.
200000 / 25 = 8000.
A / P = 9261 / 8000.

Step 2: Take cube root for 3 years:
Since A / P = (1 + R/100)³:
9261 / 8000 = (21 / 20)³ ⟹ 1 + R/100 = 21 / 20.

Step 3: Solve for R:
R/100 = 21/20 - 1 = 1/20 ⟹ R = (1/20) × 100 = 5%.
questions.trick: Cube Recognition: 8000 = 20³ and 9261 = 21³! 20 becomes 21 in 1 year ⟹ 1 unit increase on 20 = 1/20 = 5% in 3 seconds!

questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 61. What is the difference between the highest and lowest numbers?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Set up the 5 consecutive odd numbers:
Since the average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 61, the middle (3rd) number is 61.
The 5 numbers are: 57, 59, 61, 63, 65.

Step 2: Find the difference:
Highest number = 65.
Lowest number = 57.
Difference = 65 - 57 = 8.
questions.trick: Universal Consecutive Gap Shortcut: For any n consecutive odd (or even) numbers, the difference between the highest and lowest is ALWAYS 2 × (n - 1). Here n = 5 ⟹ Diff = 2 × (5 - 1) = 8. The average 61 is irrelevant!

questions.question: In an innings of 108 runs, a batsman hit 9 boundaries (fours) and 3 sixes. Find the percentage of runs scored by running between the wickets.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Calculate runs scored in boundaries:
9 boundaries (fours) = 9 × 4 = 36 runs.
3 sixes = 3 × 6 = 18 runs.
Total runs from boundaries = 36 + 18 = 54 runs.

Step 2: Runs scored by running:
Total runs = 108.
Runs by running = 108 - 54 = 54 runs.

Step 3: Percentage of runs by running:
Percentage = (54 / 108) × 100% = (1 / 2) × 100% = 50%.
questions.trick: Half-Score Inspection: 36 + 18 = 54, which is exactly half of 108 ⟹ Remaining half must be 50%! Answer marked in 2 seconds!

questions.question: A and B invest in a business in the ratio 4:5. After 10 months, B leaves the business after withdrawing his investment. In the first year (12 months), the business made a total profit of Rs. 49,000. What is B's share of the profit?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Calculate profit sharing ratio:
Profit ratio = (Investment of A × Time of A) : (Investment of B × Time of B)
A stayed for full 12 months ⟹ A's weight = 4 × 12 = 48.
B stayed for 10 months ⟹ B's weight = 5 × 10 = 50.
Ratio A : B = 48 : 50 = 24 : 25.

Step 2: Total ratio units:
Total units = 24 + 25 = 49 units.

Step 3: Calculate B's share:
49 units = Rs. 49,000 ⟹ 1 unit = Rs. 1,000.
B's share = 25 × 1,000 = Rs. 25,000.
questions.trick: Unit Simplification: Ratio = 48 : 50 ⟹ Sum = 98 units (or 24 : 25 ⟹ Sum = 49 units). Since total profit is Rs. 49,000, 1 unit = Rs. 1,000 ⟹ B's share = 25 × 1000 = Rs. 25,000!

questions.question: Find the smallest number which is a perfect square and is divisible by 6, 10, 15, and 30.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find the LCM of 6, 10, 15, and 30:
6 = 2 × 3
10 = 2 × 5
15 = 3 × 5
30 = 2 × 3 × 5
LCM(6, 10, 15, 30) = 30 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 5¹.

Step 2: Make it a perfect square:
For a number to be a perfect square, all exponents of prime factors must be even.
Multiply by 2 × 3 × 5 = 30:
Smallest square = 30 × 30 = 900.

Step 3: Verification:
900 = 30² (perfect square).
900 / 6 = 150, 900 / 10 = 90, 900 / 15 = 60, 900 / 30 = 30.
questions.trick: Option Elimination: 400 is not divisible by 6 (400/6 is not integer). 2500 is not divisible by 3. 1600 is not divisible by 3. Only 900 is divisible by 3 and is a perfect square! Option B without LCM!
